# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 13 (Bi-Vb Pc13)

**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 13
**Title (English, from literature):** Meeting a man in the open

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ajjhokāsasallapana-sikkhāpada* is the thirteenth expiation (*pācittiya*) rule in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule provides that a nun incurs an offense requiring confession if she stands or converses alone with a man out in the open (*ajjhokāse*, glossed as uncovered or in places such as streets, dead-ends, or crossroads) while seeking privacy [Hüsken 1997]. In her analysis of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, Ute Hüsken observes that the rule's non-offense (*anāpatti*) clause—which exempts a nun who does not actively seek seclusion—fits awkwardly with a rule explicitly prohibiting interactions in unsecluded (*appaticchanna*), public settings, suggesting that the exemption formula was mechanically adopted from the preceding rules (*pācittiya* 11 and 12) [Hüsken 1997].

 DharmaNexus confirms substantial Pali-internal text reuse across adjacent and related rules of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*—most notably with *pācittiya* 11, 12, and 14—and records machine-aligned parallels with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus].
